subject: AcreetionOS Update — June 18, 2026
body:
Our continuous integration pipeline has just been fine-tuned again, building on the recent introduction of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest ISO images, which significantly boosts the reliability and efficiency of our release process. This improvement is a crucial step towards making our release process more robust, and you can read more about the details of this change on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Development 
The development team has been working hard to ensure that our pipeline is stable and efficient, and these recent changes are a testament to that effort. With the introduction of per-pipeline staging directories, we can avoid publish races between concurrent builds, making the whole process more reliable. You can learn more about our development process and how to get involved on our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html.

Community 
The community has been active in discussing the latest developments, including the release of Emacs 31.1 and the latest stable kernel set. We encourage all users to stay up-to-date with the latest security updates, which can be found on our website at https://acreetionos.org/. For those looking to dive deeper into the world of AcreetionOS, our documentation page at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html is a great resource, covering everything from installation to configuration. 

Tip of the day 
If you're looking for a quick way to get started with AcreetionOS, be sure to check out our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html, which provides a brief overview of the project and its goals. From there, you can explore our website and learn more about what we're working on and how you can get involved.
